messages.content: Write a customer testimonial section for the website of a log aggregation service. Around 200 words.

## What teams say

> "The old routine was two in the morning, forty boxes, forty grep windows. When checkout fell over in March we had the bad deploy in eleven minutes, instead of tailing files until it got light out."
>
> **Priya Raghunathan** — Staff SRE, Wexler Freight

> "I blocked out a full sprint for the migration and warned everyone it would be tight. The agent was in production on day four. We shut the old Elasticsearch cluster down the following Tuesday and nobody has asked for it back."
>
> **Daniel Okonkwo** — Platform Lead, Corvid Health

> "Our bill went from $18k a month to about $4,200, and that was on 30% more ingest. Retention was the part that caught me off guard: seven days became ninety. The quarterly argument over which services get to keep their logs has just stopped happening."
>
> **Mireille Fontaine** — Director of Engineering, Halden Systems

> "Support wants a customer's request trace maybe twice a week. It used to arrive in my queue as a ticket. Now they pull it themselves, and I hear from them only when something is actually broken."
>
> **Sam Weatherly** — Backend Engineer, Tessellate

*Names, companies, and figures above are placeholders. Swap in real, approved quotes before publishing.*
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

## What teams say

> "It used to be a two a.m. ritual: forty terminal tabs, forty greps, one theory at a time. When checkout went down in March we had the bad deploy in eleven minutes and I was back in bed before the sun came up."
>
> **Priya Raghunathan** — Staff SRE, Wexler Freight

> "I budgeted a whole sprint for the cutover and told everyone to expect pain. The agent was live in production on day four. We powered off the old Elasticsearch cluster the following Tuesday, and no one has asked for it since."
>
> **Daniel Okonkwo** — Platform Lead, Corvid Health

> "We were paying $18k a month. We now pay around $4,200, and that's with 30% more ingest. Retention is the part I didn't expect: seven days went to ninety. The quarterly fight over whose services get to keep their logs has simply stopped."
>
> **Mireille Fontaine** — Director of Engineering, Halden Systems

> "Support needs a customer's request trace maybe twice a week. It used to land in my queue as a ticket. They pull it themselves now, and I hear from them only when there's a real outage."
>
> **Sam Weatherly** — Backend Engineer, Tessellate
